newsitem.title: USA: FTC chairman says Staples deal 'fixable'.
newsitem.headline: FTC chairman says Staples deal 'fixable'.

text.p: Federal Trade Commission Chairman Robert Pitofsky said Thursday a proposed merger between Staples Inc. and Office Depot Inc. is potentially "fixable" and his agency may act within 10 to 14 days.
"Is it fixable?" he said, repeating a reporter's question. "Yeah, it's fixable. I'm really just speculating here. I don't know what they're offering or what we'd require."
Pitofsky, talking with a reporter after a speech to the Consumer Federation of America, said it was premature to comment because the five commissioners had not seen any proposal.

Any negotiations between the companies and the FTC happen at the staff level for now, with the final product brought to the comission. Even taking the time for those negotiations into account, Pitofsky said the commission would act relatively quickly.
"There's no reason for us to sit around with this more than 10 days, two weeks, something like that," he said.
The commission voted 4-1 last week to reject the proposed merger. Two days later, the two stores reached an agreement to sell 63 stores to OfficeMax for about $109 million.

At the time, company officials said they believed the sale would satisfy regulators. The sale of the stores would make OfficeMax a competitor in the Washington-Baltimore area, where it now has no stores, improve its position in Los Angeles and move it into many other markets across the country.
The commissioners still must examine a final agreement for the divestiture, which had not been reached by Thursday.
